title: chore(deps): bump anyio from 4.14.1 to 4.14.2 in the pip group across 1 directory
body:
Bumps the pip group with 1 update in the / directory: [anyio](https://github.com/agronholm/anyio). Updates `anyio` from 4.14.1 to 4.14.2
Release notes

Sourced from anyio's releases.

4.14.2

  • Changed ByteReceiveStream.receive() implementations to raise a ValueError when max_bytes is not a positive integer (#1191)
  • Fixed CapacityLimiter.total_tokens rejecting float("inf") when the limiter was instantiated outside of an event loop. The adapter setter checked for infinity by identity (value is math.inf), so only the exact math.inf singleton was accepted, while every backend setter (using math.isinf()) accepts any positive infinity (#1189; PR by @​greymoth-jp).
  • Fixed to_process.run_sync() deadlocking when the worker function writes enough data to sys.stderr to fill the (undrained) pipe buffer. The worker process now redirects sys.stderr to os.devnull as well, matching the documented behavior
  • Fixed TLSStream.wrap() matching an internationalized (unicode) host name against the peer certificate using IDNA 2003 (via the standard library) instead of IDNA 2008, which could cause the host name to be matched against the wrong certificate (#1208)
  • Fixed anyio.open_process() (and run_process()) ignoring the extra_groups argument, as it mistakenly passed the value of the group argument instead (#1209)
  • Fixed CapacityLimiter.acquire_nowait() and CapacityLimiter.acquire_nowait_on_behalf_of() raising trio.WouldBlock instead of anyio.WouldBlock on the trio backend when there are no tokens available (#1218)
  • Fixed CapacityLimiter on the asyncio backend over-granting tokens (borrowed_tokens exceeding total_tokens and available_tokens going negative) when a non-blocking acquire was made in the window between a token being released and the notified waiter resuming. The freed token is now reserved for the woken waiter right away, so the non-blocking acquire correctly raises WouldBlock (#1170; PR by @​gaoflow)
  • Fixed unnecessary CPU spin when delivering cancellation from CancelScope on asyncio under certain conditions, including improper cancel scope nesting (#1111)
Commits
  • c384f99 Bumped up the version
  • dbba29d Fixed 100% CPU spin on cancel scope misuse (#1217)
  • 6bbc6c3 Fix CapacityLimiter over-granting tokens on asyncio (#1172)
  • 6f82b25 Refactored TestTLSStream.test_receive_invalid_max_bytes() to be less flaky
  • be24b04 Relaxed timeouts to fix test flakiness
  • 8113506 Fix test flakiness caused by slow callback duration logging
  • 1e988b6 Fixed CapacityLimiter raising trio.WouldBlock instead of anyio.WouldBlock (#1...
  • 44713f3 Pin setup-uv to a commit sha across downstream jobs (#1213)
  • f1b7301 Fixed stderr writes in a worker subprocess causing a deadlock (#1207)
  • 212be93 Fix flaky test_tcp_listener_same_port using a hardcoded port (#1206)
  • Additional commits viewable in compare view

Deprecations

Two API surfaces now emit DeprecationWarning ahead of their removal in v2. Nothing is removed in 1.x, and the warnings fire only when the deprecated API is called - importing the modules stays silent.

Fix `_read_issue_conversation_locks_batch` rejecting valid repository slugs whose owner and repository names match. Validate the presence of exactly two non-empty path components instead of requiring different names.

**Expected output**: Valid equal-name slugs use the normal authoritative batch read. Empty snapshots return `[]` without an API call. Missing or additional path components fail before transport. Incomplete lock evidence remains fail-closed.

## Implementation and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh`: replace the owner/name inequality with a structural two-component guard; leave GraphQL bindings, response validation, lock verification and mutations unchanged.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-auto-dispatch-conversation-lock.sh`: extend existing mocked-GitHub and isolated-marker fixtures. Cover equal names, empty inventory, malformed slugs and missing batch evidence.

v4.13.7

Security fixes

This release includes a fix for the following security issue:

hono/jsx renders plain strings unescaped in boundary components, leading to XSS

Affects: Suspense, ErrorBoundary, and Context.Provider in hono/jsx, and renderToString() / renderToReadableStream() in hono/jsx/dom/server. Fixes missing HTML escaping for a plain string placed directly as a child or fallback of these components, or as the root value of the server rendering functions, so untrusted strings could be emitted as markup. Users who render untrusted strings inside Suspense, ErrorBoundary, or Context.Provider, or pass them directly to hono/jsx/dom/server, are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.

title: GH#32259: preserve Pulse refill budget after label maintenance
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to merged PR #32262. Its fixed 300-second consolidation-backfill timeout still lets optional maintenance consume the post-label dispatch window. Use the *existing outer stage watchdog* with a deadline computed from the current cycle's remaining time minus the refill admission reserve and a 5-second watchdog margin. Apply the same bound to trusted NMR reconciliation, which also runs before the refill. Defer these optional stages when the budget is exhausted or untrustworthy; retain early dispatch, REST-core gates, and the refill's existing admission check.

For #32259. This PR completes the narrowed budget/productivity direction in the maintainer review; it does not assert that backfill was responsible for the reported 22-minute freeze.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh`: compute a shared pre-refill timeout from the cycle clock and pass it to the existing NMR watchdog; remove PR #32262's redundant fixed substage wrapper.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`: bound or defer both optional pre-refill stages and log budget-based deferral.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh`: cover normal, constrained, exhausted, and invalid 1800-second cycle budgets.

## Runtime Testing

- Risk: high (Pulse scheduling); no production Pulse was run on this macOS host.
- Existing focused checks: stage wiring 57/57, cycle gates 50/50, consolidation dispatch 62/62, singleton lock 8/8.
- ShellCheck on all three changed files, shfmt on touched sections, changed-file lint and `git diff --check`: pass (engine has pre-existing shfmt-only differences outside this patch).
- Acceptance at runtime after deployment: a slow label-maintenance or trusted NMR stage must time out or be deferred before the configured post-label refill admission threshold; inspect `Stage timeout`/`deferred` and `Post-label dispatch_max` telemetry for the same cycle. Attribution of the historical freeze remains unproven.

## Rollback

Revert this follow-up commit to restore PR #32262's existing fixed-timeout policy; no persistent state migration is involved.

body:
## Summary

- Route bounded `playwright` subagent operations to connected GPT-6 Luna xhigh from standard/thinking OpenCode sessions without changing the global model tiers.
- On unavailable Luna, choose connected Sol medium or the verified parent model and effort; preserve explicit pins, same-model effort ceilings, and child route across turns.
- Keep browser side effects under parent authority: no automatic replay or capability escalation after browser execution, and reject model drift.

Resolves #32281

## Files and pattern

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/subagent-effort-handlers.mjs`: task-specific child route alongside existing tier, parent, and reasoning-clamp hooks.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-subagent-effort.mjs`: hook integration fixtures for Luna, fallback, parent clamp, pin, and model drift.
- `.agents/reference/agent-routing.md`, `.agents/tools/browser/playwright.md`, and `README.md`: operator guidance and explicit scope.

## Runtime Testing

- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-subagent-effort.mjs` — 36/36 passed; exercises the actual chat-message/params routing hooks with runtime-shaped provider and parent-session evidence.
- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-credential-scrub.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-subagent-effort.mjs` — 89/89 passed.

- No live authenticated site was used; browser task reliability and cost savings remain outcomes to measure, not claims of this PR.

## Decisions

The browser-specific xhigh setting is deliberately separate from the simple-tier Luna-low default. body:
## Summary

Integrate a persistent per-user OpenCode V1 owner with normal aidevops setup/update. Keep Desktop and attached TUI conversations on one SQLite owner while retaining explicit direct access to existing histories.

- Reconcile a loopback-only launchd/systemd user service after runtime/plugin deployment. Fresh history-free installations can opt into the managed default automatically; existing identity, routing and disabled state survive updates.
- Keep owner startup in a private staged runtime, including its Python modules, so deployment-alias replacement cannot remove its launcher.
- Verify manager PID, exclusive owner lock, listener ancestry, health and version before attaching. Do not force-restart active owners, migrate databases, or edit private Desktop state.
- Preserve Tabby exact-session recovery; document explicit managed/direct commands, rollback and manual Desktop server/project selection.

## Implementation context

Core files: `.agents/scripts/opencode-service-helper.py`, `opencode_service_state.py`, `opencode_service_lifecycle.py` and `opencode-launcher-helper.sh`; setup integration in `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh` and `setup.sh`. Reference pattern: the existing foreground server/attach launcher and its exclusive-owner checks. Guides: `.agents/reference/opencode-service.md`, `opencode-maintenance.md`, and `README.md`.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified on macOS with OpenCode 1.18.32.
- Verified TUI → Desktop → TUI history, Build+ with GPT-6 Astra and a completed `aidevops_hook_status` tool call.
- Unchanged reinstall retained the owner PID; disable → install stayed disabled; enable/restart retained the conversation. This closeout issued no owner restart command. A final post-merge check observed an intervening owner restart (manager exit 143, cause not established); health and preserved-session attachment passed again afterward.
- Re-ran a real PTY attachment through the final refactored CLI: prior reply and Build+ visible, live server connection, zero session-database handles in the attached TUI.
- Passed 28 focused service tests, 12 server-launcher tests, 32 launcher tests, 2 setup-stage tests and 79 tool-install assertions. Packaging regressions cover the staged CLI after deployment-source removal and execution through the deployment symlink.
- Changed-file lint, ShellCheck, Bash 3.2 compatibility and secret checks passed. Qlty 0.643.0 reports no smells for the three new runtime Python files after the required CI complexity repair; no thresholds or exclusions were relaxed.
- Linux/WSL2 service contracts are mock-tested only. No native Windows support, actual logout/reboot test or full real setup/update rerun is claimed.

## Review and decisions

- Independent closeout review repaired stale executable-path reconciliation while preserving the active-definition-change guard.
- Persisting disabled desired state before attempting stop is intentional: a failed stop remains an error, health reports the actual owner, and later setup must not silently undo the user's opt-out.

title: GH#32360: guard recovery storage permissions before archival
body:
## Summary

Resolves #32360.

Prevent recovery archival from silently failing on a non-writable store, and refuse root archival of another user's worktree before creating storage directories.

## Evidence and cause

A user-scoped cleanup installation repeatedly reported `cwd-visibility-degraded` followed by `recoverable-archive-failed` / `archive-copy-failed`, including candidates with merged-PR evidence and clear ownership guards. The configured recovery directory was owned by root with mode 0755 and was not writable by the cleanup account. The archive producer's suppressed mkdir failures obscured this actionable cause. Local ownership was repaired separately with explicit operator authorization; this PR does not change filesystem ownership automatically.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh`: add a preflight before recovery-root creation and producer-lock acquisition. Check the nearest existing parent for write/search access; reject root operating on another user's worktree. Emit specific structured audit reasons and an operator-facing diagnostic. title: GH#32368: prevent interrupted recovery archive growth
body:
## Problem

Resolves #32368.

The archive-first cleanup producer copies entire worktrees before pruning regenerable caches. A bounded cleanup timeout can interrupt this copy before metadata or `archive-complete` is written. Subsequent attempts create new timestamped buckets for the same source, so a cleanup intended to relieve disk pressure instead multiplies partial dependency trees. An observed installation accumulated tens of GiB this way. A separate ownership repair exposed this producer failure; permission diagnostics alone do not resolve it.

## Implementation

- `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_archive_copy.py`: exclude only proven ignored, untracked, allowlisted cache directories before copy IO, including nested cache roots beneath broader ignored directories. Preserve symlinks, tracked paths, and unknown ignored data. Stop on unavailable Git evidence.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-recovery-cache-policy.py`: expose copy, reservation, and completed-snapshot comparison through the existing fail-closed mode dispatcher.
- `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh`: reserve one attempt per physical source identity under the existing producer lock before copying. Interrupted attempts cannot create additional buckets. Reuse completed snapshots only after existing Git identity validation and a current user-content/staged-state comparison.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-removal-audit-lib.sh`: regression coverage for pre-copy cache filtering, tracked/unknown data preservation, bounded repeated attempts, safe completed reuse, and refusal after new user data appears.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh`: copy the new archive module into the existing isolated profile fixture so its recoverable-cleanup path exercises the complete dependency set.
- `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`: document interruption and operator-recovery semantics.

## Safety and scope

Existing source-removal guards remain unchanged. Unknown legacy partial archives are not automatically deleted or adopted. New incomplete attempts retain their reservation and require operator review; this intentionally pauses an unsafe retry rather than erasing possibly unique data. The original source remains intact on failure. This change bounds retries for an unchanged physical source; it is not authority to delete arbitrary home-directory data or bypass active-worktree protections.

The existing archive finalization still copies Git administrative state and rewrites the archived `.git` pointer before publication. Completed-reuse comparison therefore uses archive-local staged state, not the original live index.

## Verification

- Existing worktree-removal audit suite, including new cases and merged permission guard: 53/53 passed.
- Recovery lifecycle suite: 53/53 passed in a non-root, network-isolated Linux container with read-only source and executable temporary fixture storage. The shared multi-user host has degraded process visibility; the baseline fixture fails there too.
- Profile README boundary suite: 27/27 passed after fixing the fixture dependency found by CI.
- Changed-file local lint and ShellCheck passed.
- Python compile and Ruff check passed; whitespace diff check passed.
- Operational storage cleanup and live deployment verification remain separate from the code checks above.

## Reference pattern

Use the existing recovery producer lock, Git identity validation, and cache allowlist (`worktree_recovery_cache_policy_common.py`). No new cleanup scheduler or broad-delete policy is introduced.

title: GH#32375: authenticated read-only browser QA journey
body:
Resolves #32375

## Summary

Adds `browser-qa-helper.sh journey --config FILE --environment NAME`, an opt-in authenticated **read-only** browser journey. Existing `run|screenshot|links|a11y|smoke|stability` behaviour is unchanged. The worker's original version was taken over interactively: it failed Qlty and did not meet several acceptance criteria.

- **Split into small modules** (all Qlty smells cleared: 0 in new files, previously 4):
  - `browser-qa-journey-config.mjs`: versioned schema validation that runs before browser launch. It covers exact origin, exact endpoint paths, bounded timeouts, own-property step lookup and credential env names. Credential values are removed from the process environment before launch.
  - `browser-qa-journey-guard.mjs`: context-level network/navigation guard.
  - `browser-qa-journey-steps.mjs`: lookup table of declarative step handlers (no config-supplied code); assertions re-check until the action timeout.
  - `browser-qa-journey.mjs`: per-viewport lifecycle and report.
- **Write boundary fixes**:
  - The previous off-origin check used `request.headers().cookie`, which Playwright never populates, so it never fired. It is replaced by `allHeaders()` credential detection, blocking of off-origin main-frame navigation, and a `framenavigated` check for redirect hops.
  - The sign-in submission is fetched with `maxRedirects: 0`, so an off-origin (including 307 body-replay) redirect is blocked before credentials are replayed.
  - Login must be POST/PUT/PATCH, so credentials never travel in a query string.
  - WebSockets are never connected to the server; blocked sockets are reported as `webSocketsBlocked`.
- **Lifecycle**: service workers and downloads are blocked. Sign-out uses the context's request client with its own timeout, so it still runs after step failure or an exhausted run budget. There is a whole-run `runTimeoutMs` plus a hard fuse.
- **Report**: per-step route pattern (`/items/:id`), console/page-error counts, guard counters. Error text keeps only its first line, has query strings stripped and credentials masked. No screenshots, traces, storage state, cookies or page bodies.
- Docs: `tools/browser/browser-qa.md` (schema, boundary, limits, secret-injection example); `workflows/ui-verification.md` still prefers a repository's existing E2E suite.
- `test-browser-qa-helper.sh` `magick` PATH stubs (from the original worker commit): `enforce_screenshot_guardrails` exits early when neither `sips` nor `magick` exists (`browser-qa-helper-core.sh:152`). The stubs keep the existing guardrail tests hermetic on Linux runners.

## Testing

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-browser-qa-journey.sh`: 21/21 pass. It uses two disposable local fixture apps (different ports, credentials and journey definitions) with real Chromium and covers:
  - desktop+mobile login → assert (text/count/attribute/modal/media src/overflow) → logout
  - the second environment passes on its own sessions with no cookie reuse (`foreignCookies:0`)
  - a blocked non-`/api` POST never reaches the app
  - wrong-origin link navigation and an off-origin 307 sign-in redirect are both blocked (`offOriginHits:0`)
  - a timeout still signs out
  - wrong password fails
  - a WebSocket never reaches the server
  - validation rejects unknown version, origin with path, missing credentials, protocol-relative path, unknown/prototype step type and GET sign-in
  - no password or `sid=` value appears in any output

  Browser cases skip when no Playwright runtime is installed.
- Mutation checks: disabling write blocking, off-origin navigation blocking, or WebSocket blocking each makes the corresponding tests fail.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-browser-qa-helper.sh`: 16/16 pass.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`: all passed (ShellCheck, shfmt, secretlint, markdownlint, complexity ratchets).
- `qlty smells` on the changed files and `qlty-new-file-gate-helper.sh new-files --base origin/main --head HEAD`: 0 smells.

## Runtime Testing

`runtime-verified`: the CLI entry point (`browser-qa-helper.sh journey`) was exercised end-to-end against the local disposable fixture apps with the framework-owned Playwright 1.63 runtime.

## Review

Critical-risk auth boundary. Both model-backed advisory routes (thinking and standard tiers) were unavailable in this session, so the review was a manual pass against the acceptance criteria. That pass found and fixed the WebSocket bypass and the GET sign-in gap. Out of scope, documented as limits: MFA/CAPTCHA, off-origin SSO sign-in, CSRF-token-protected sign-out.

body:
## Summary

Anthropic OAuth prompt-cache stability and first-prompt context reduction for OpenCode 1 (1.18.x) and OpenCode 2 (2.0.x), preserving the OAuth compliance wire shape (system = [billing header, Claude Code identity]; framework text redistributed into the first user message; tool-name normalisation, TAG_RENAMES, agent__intent, cch body-hash signing).

- A1 (provider-auth-body.mjs): cch signing now uses a unique per-request header sentinel so the hash is computed and written only at the billing-header position. Previously a first-match replace could hit a placeholder copy quoted in message history (messages serialize before system), producing a wrong hash and a per-turn cache rewrite.
- A2: carry overflow system-block cache_control onto the redistributed prefix block, clamped to Anthropic's 4-breakpoint maximum.
- A3: redistribution diagnostics log suffix (kept/sha/cache/session); OC1 session id read from host request headers via hostSessionID() before buildRequestHeaders strips them.
- B1 (ttsr.mjs): in-place system-array mutation (OC1 ignores reassignment); Intent + Quality blocks restored; plugin greeting default-off in OC1 (AGENTS.md fallback greets, keeps the turn-1/turn-2 prefix identical) and default-on in OC2 (isolated config home has no AGENTS.md and only the plugin knows the V2 runtime version); AIDEVOPS_PLUGIN_SESSION_GREETING=1|0 overrides.

title: GH#32455: stop binding mutable trusted linked-source content in approval snapshots
body:
## Summary

Approval snapshots stopped going stale when supervisor dashboards that link the approved PR/issue refresh themselves (GH#32455). A new `trusted-sources` linked-source profile is now the default for signing and verification.

Resolves #32455

## What changed

- `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh`: new `trusted-sources` profile (`_approval_snapshot_v2_linked_source_content`). A linked source whose repository equals the target repository **and** whose `author_association` is `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR` binds identity (repo, number, ids, author, association) with `content_bound: false`, omitting mutable `title`/`body`/`state`. All other sources (untrusted association or other repository) bind full content plus `content_bound: true`. Marked `#aidevops:trust-boundary`.
- `.agents/scripts/approval-helper-continuity.sh`: `_approval_classify_digest_mismatch` first tries the previous `stable` profile (exact digest match only → `STABLE_MATCH`), then the pre-GH#29009 `legacy` profile, then locked-issue continuity against both the current and stable snapshots. Existing signatures keep verifying exactly as before.
- `.agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh`: verification uses `trusted-sources` first and accepts `STABLE_MATCH`/`LEGACY_MATCH`; the redundant legacy rebuild was removed because profiles differ only in linked references, so the head/base check is profile-independent.
- `.agents/scripts/source_access_core.py`: native signing snapshot mirrors the new projection (byte parity with the shell oracle).

## Trust rationale

Write-trusted authors of the same repository already hold authority to change the target itself; their dashboard text is not approval scope. Association is repository-relative, so cross-repository sources stay content-bound. Association drift (e.g. OWNER → CONTRIBUTOR) changes the digest and stales the approval.

## Verification

title: GH#32468: Latest Anthropic tier fallbacks and OpenAI-vs-Anthropic provider-family model A/B
body:
## Summary

- Anthropic OAuth is available again, so its same-tier fallbacks move to the latest generation: Haiku 4.5 (unchanged, still the latest Haiku), **Sonnet 5 @ low** and **Opus 5.5 @ medium**. OpenAI stays primary, so the shared default does not change without A/B evidence.
- `model-ab-helper.mjs` can now compare **OpenAI vs Anthropic as provider families** on background workers:
  - **Provider-family arms:** each arm has a route for every tier, so worker escalations and the worker's OpenCode subagent delegations stay with the assigned provider unless it is unavailable.
  - **All-tier enrollment:** `new-auto-dispatch-issues`.
  - **Start preset:** `start OWNER/REPO --preset openai-anthropic` builds the arms from the routing table, with a 7-day default window.
  - **Crossover reporting:** `off_arm_models` / `off_arm_issues` per arm.
- Plugin config load now drops legacy `(via aidevops)` Anthropic model overrides written before GH#32447. They set `tool_call: false`, text-only input and zero cost on `claude-haiku-4-5` / `sonnet-4-6` / `opus-4-6`, and were still present in a real user `opencode.json`.
- Pricing: exact Anthropic entries (Opus 4.5–5.5 incl. Fast, Fable 5/5.1, Sonnet 5, Haiku 4.5) come before the generic family keys. Previously `opus-4` priced Opus 4.5–4.8 at the retired $15/$75 rate. Source: the OpenCode models.dev catalog, not revalidated against Anthropic's pricing page (recorded in `_anthropic_source`).

## Why (evidence)

- The #32353 review ([comment](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/32353#issuecomment-5851919751)) found the 48 h standard-only Luna/Terra trial enrolled only **2 issues**. Most standard issues were solved interactively, and the worker-solved issues were mostly thinking-tier, which that enrollment excluded. It also found an unattributed arm crossover on #32362. Hence: all-tier enrollment, a 168 h cap, and off-arm reporting.
- Live headless smoke tests on 2026-09-27 passed for `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 --variant low` and `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 --variant medium`. Haiku and Sonnet 5 also completed a read-tool call. `opencode models anthropic --verbose` shows Sonnet 5 / Opus 5.5 support adaptive `low…max` effort; Haiku 4.5 has only `high|max`, so its variant is left unset.

## Compatibility

- Legacy standard-only arms, receipts and configs validate and behave as before. The ended trial's report runs unchanged and now shows `off_arm_issues: 1` for #32362.
- The launcher now passes `--tier` instead of `--continuation-only`. For standard-only arms the helper maps non-standard tiers to continuation-only, as before. Unknown tier values still pass `--continuation-only`.
- On retry, route verification now compares only the arm's primary model and effort per tier. Shipped fallback-order changes between releases no longer fail an in-flight assignment.

## Verification

- `node --test .agents/scripts/tests/test-model-ab-helper.mjs` → 7/7, including the new provider-family case.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-model-ab-dispatch.sh` → the legacy case passes and the new thinking-tier provider-family case passes.

title: GH#23846: keep Nostr VPN nvpn current via aidevops update
body:
## Summary

Nostr VPN (`mmalmi/nostr-vpn`, app 4.1.16 from nostrvpn.org) embeds its own FIPS fork, so aidevops now keeps that stack current instead of the standalone `jmcorgan/fips` daemon.

- `nostr-vpn-helper.sh update [--check]`:
  - keeps `/usr/local/bin/nvpn` on the same version as the app-managed daemon, using `install-cli` from the app helper
  - reports app updates, which the app applies itself through its verified in-app updater
  - uses `nvpn update` on CLI-only hosts; nvpn refuses unverified releases
- `nostr-vpn-helper.sh conflicts` / `nvpn-status`:
  - detect the NetBird/nvpn UDP `51820` clash
  - flag a leftover `com.fips.daemon`
- `setup.sh`: adds a bounded non-interactive stage (`AIDEVOPS_SETUP_NOSTR_VPN_TIMEOUT`, default 120s) plus an interactive step. Both **update only when Nostr VPN is already installed**. They never install Nostr VPN, replace the app, write the root helper, or change nvpn config.
- `services/networking/nostr-vpn.md` changes:
  - nvpn is now the recommended stack and standalone FIPS is marked legacy
  - new NetBird coexistence table
  - enrollment flow
  - root-helper hygiene check

## Evidence

- Live on this Mac: `netstat -anv -p udp` shows `netbird:58415` bound to `*.51820`, while `nvpn status` reports `configured_listen_port: 51820` and `listen_port: 0`. The helper reports `CONFLICT: nvpn and NetBird both use UDP 51820`.
- `nvpn update --app` is download-only upstream (`crates/nostr-vpn-cli/src/updater.rs`: App mode → print downloaded, no install). The app has its own verified in-app hashtree updater (upstream CHANGELOG).
- aidevops never writes to the root-run `/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/to.nostrvpn.nvpn`; only the user-owned `nvpn` CLI is refreshed.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on the helper, test, `tool-install.sh` and `setup.sh`: clean
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-nostr-vpn-helper.sh`: 12/12 pass, including 2 new stub tests (CLI lock-step install; NetBird port conflict)
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`: exit 0

title: GH#32362: redact secret-helper credentials from process-list Bash output
body:
## Summary

Adds exact registered-value redaction at the OpenCode tool-output boundary. Plaintext values already held locally (aidevops credential files, plugin env values under registered or sensitive names) are matched longest-first anywhere in output. Values injected by secret-helper.sh run (including gopass-only values) are matched through a keyed HMAC digest registry (length plus digest only, 0600 in a 0700 dir; no plaintext stored). Applied to Bash/all tool output, title and persisted metadata in tool.execute.after before the pattern scrub, and to bounded-operation captures before storage so offset/limit windows cannot split a value. New files: registered-value-redaction.mjs, redaction-digest-registry.py, tests/test-registered-value-redaction.mjs. Limitations: live TUI streaming preview during a running Bash call is outside plugin hooks (final persisted part and model delivery are scrubbed); a digest-only value glued to other token characters without a delimiter is not matched. Note: the runtime secret-read guard blocks Read/Edit of any basename containing 'secret' (and .gitignore ignores *secret*), so the secret-helper.sh call sites were added by an anchored three-insertion script (unique-anchor check, no content printed); the diff is 16 added lines and was independently reviewed.



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-interactive-operation.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/registered-value-redaction.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-registered-value-redaction.mjs, .agents/scripts/redaction-digest-registry.py, .agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh

title: GH#32484: Route standard tier to GPT-6 Sol low with verified GPT-6 pricing
body:
## Summary

Resolves #32484

- **Standard tier → GPT-6 Sol low.** `configs/model-routing-table.json` and `aidevops.defaults.jsonc` now route `standard` to `openai/gpt-6-sol` (low), then Terra low, GLM-5.2 and Sonnet 5. Sol remains the thinking primary at medium. OpenAI Standard pricing (checked 2026-09-27) lists Sol at $2 / $0.20 / $10 per 1M tokens (input/cached/output) versus Terra's $2 / $0.20 / $12. Terra therefore cost more for an older generation. The #32353 Luna/Terra trial was inconclusive (n=1 per arm), so this is a price-and-generation decision, not outcome evidence.
- **Verified GPT-6 pricing.** `model-pricing.json`, the shell fallback in `shared-model-tier.sh` and the plugin `FALLBACK_PRICING` now include gpt-6-sol (2 / 10 / 0.20 / 2.50) and gpt-6-luna (0.10 / 0.50 / 0.01 / 0.125). The pricing version is now `2026-09-27.2`. Sol Pro keeps the unknown-model estimate.
- **Multi-tier model lookup fix.** Sol now appears in two tiers, so a first-tier-wins lookup would silently turn a thinking dispatch into standard/low.
  - `model_tier_for_model <model> [preferred_tier]` keeps the preferred tier whenever that tier lists the model.
  - The headless adaptive selection (`headless-runtime-run.sh`) and the tier downgrade check (`headless-runtime-model.sh`) pass the requested tier.
  - Runner and cron bare model pins prefer `thinking`, so existing Sol pins keep medium effort.
  - OpenCode `routingTierForModel` matches the observed variant, which keeps root-routing telemetry correct.
- **Guidance.**
  - `reference/agent-routing.md` no longer restates concrete model names; it points to the routing table.
  - It adds primary-session context-efficiency guidance. 14-day local telemetry put ~90% of estimated spend in primary sessions, with reasoning under 1% of tokens.
  - `tools/context/model-routing.md` is updated with the new mapping, rationale and GPT-6 prices.

## Verification

- `node --test` passed (exit 0) on: `test-observability-pricing`, `-cost-backfill`, `-routing-join`, `test-model-routing` (new multi-tier variant test), `test-subagent-effort`, `test-specialist-advisor`, `test-model-limits`, `test-gpt56-context-config`, `test-routing-feedback`, and `scripts/tests/test-model-ab-helper.mjs`.

title: GH#32498: OpenCode V2 parity: load framework AGENTS.md, sanitize service env, leave Tabby recovery dirs
body:
## Summary

OpenCode V2 (`opencode2`) was not loading everything OpenCode V1 loads, and its greeting could go missing. This PR fixes three parity gaps found while testing GH#32444:

1. **Framework guide missing in V2.** V1 loads `~/.aidevops/agents/AGENTS.md` (~6K tokens) through the `instructions` entry in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`. The isolated V2 config had only `plugins`, so V2 sessions answered faster but without the framework guide. A canary probe showed V2 loads `<config>/opencode/AGENTS.md`, so setup now links the guide there.
2. **Service inherited a session/headless environment.** The live V2 service (`serve --service`, ppid 1) had inherited an OpenCode V1 session's environment: `OPENCODE_PID`, `OPENCODE=1`, `AGENT=1`, `AIDEVOPS_OPERATION_ID`, `AIDEVOPS_TABBY_SESSION_RECOVERY`, `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_ISOLATED_DB`, and a pinned `AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR`. A headless flag inherited the same way makes `shouldInjectGreeting` return false for every session. One user session (`ses_f1f2d1520ffe…`) got 5 redistributed blocks instead of the usual 6, meaning no greeting block. The managed shim now drops that inherited state for service and TUI launches.
3. **Tabby recovery marker cwd.** Launching `opencode2` from a Tabby recovery marker directory left V2 in the marker dir. The shim now resolves the marker's project with `session-recovery-marker.mjs` and `cd`s there (falling back to `$HOME`). It never resumes the V1 session.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh`: `_setup_opencode_v2_link_framework_guide` symlinks the guide into the V2 config, called from the V2 branch of `setup_opencode_plugins`. It keeps user-authored files and symlinks pointing outside `~/.aidevops/`, and repairs stale managed links.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh`:
  - `# aidevops:opencode-v2-shim-version=2` marker, so existing shims regenerate;
  - `_setup_append_opencode_v2_session_guard` parses args (`--standalone`/`--server` keep the env; value flags are skipped) and unsets inherited OpenCode/aidevops session, worker, headless, Tabby, overlay and bundle-pin variables;
  - kept on purpose: `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`AIDEVOPS_OPENAI_API_KEY_SOURCE` for the OAuth pool, and `GITHUB_ACTIONS`;
  - Tabby marker-dir redirect for TUI launches.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/root-session-greeting-gate.mjs` (new): the V2 root-session greeting gate, moved out of `v2.mjs`. It skips child sessions silently and logs any other skip (headless env, no session lookup, lookup failure) once per session to `opencode-plugin.log`. A separate module keeps `ttsr.mjs` under the qlty complexity threshold.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs`: wires the gate and logs when `AIDEVOPS_PLUGIN_SESSION_GREETING` disables the greeting.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh`: comment only. The deploy-time restart already goes through the managed shim, which now sanitizes the env.
- Docs: `.agents/tools/opencode/opencode.md` (V1/V2 parity paragraph), `.agents/reference/context-efficiency.md` (greeting wording).

No double greeting: `~/.aidevops/agents/AGENTS.md` has no greeting text. The V1 greeting fallback lives only in `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md`.

Anthropic OAuth wire shaping (billing header plus identity in `system`, redistributed framework text, cch signing) and the OpenAI OAuth-pool path are unchanged.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-v2-setup.sh` → `OpenCode V2 setup tests passed`. New cases: link created, stale managed link repaired, user file kept, user symlink kept, shim version marker present.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-install-opencode.sh` → `84 passed, 0 failed`. New cases: inherited env dropped, `--standalone` keeps env, marker-dir cd, `$HOME` fallback, non-marker cwd kept.
- `node --test tests/test-session-start-greeting-gate.mjs` → 4/4 pass.
- The V2 adapter test (`tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs`) passes 16/16 in a mirror that has `@opencode/plugin` installed, run with an isolated HOME.
- Full plugin suite in the mirror: 986/992. The 6 failures are in the signature-footer and source-access tests and come only from the isolated HOME; rerun with the real HOME they pass 111/111. None of those files are touched here.
- `shellcheck` is clean on the changed scripts and on a generated shim. `qlty smells` reports nothing on the changed files.
- The real marker resolver maps the user's Tabby marker to its original project checkout.

## Post-merge checks

After release and `aidevops update`:
- `~/.local/bin/opencode2` contains the version-2 marker;
- `<v2 config>/opencode/AGENTS.md` links to the framework guide;
- the restarted service env has no `OPENCODE_PID`/`AIDEVOPS_*` session vars;
- a fresh V2 session shows `core/instructions` in `instruction_state` and greets once.

Resolves #32498
Ref #32444

title: GH#32510: Defer exact-tag deployment when active runtime is an ancestor of the integration mainline parent
body:
## Summary

Resolves #32510

The v3.37.3 exact-tag deployment (source PR #32474) deadlocked.

- The active runtime was hot-deployed from `b91c0a895`.
- Three more mainline merges landed before protected-main PR #32497 merged the signed release commit `dbfed4421`.
- `_verify_protected_release_integration` required the active SHA to be **exactly** a parent of the integration merge. Reconcile therefore rejected the runtime as "neither ancestry-related nor a lane-authorized squash-integrated source".
- The lane stayed in `exact-tag-deployment`. That blocked `aidevops update` ("Active exact-tag release deployment blocks generic setup") and every new release, including the pending v3.37.4 for #32493.

### Change (`.agents/scripts/version-manager-release.sh`)

- New `_protected_integration_mainline_parent` returns the non-release parent of a two-parent merge. The other parent must be exactly the signed release commit; octopus merges, non-merges and other topologies are rejected.
- `_verify_protected_release_integration` now grants the `stale-runtime/v1` deferral when the active runtime is that mainline parent **or an ancestor of it**. The merge then contains everything already deployed, so converging on protected main cannot downgrade the runtime.
- The deferral itself deploys nothing.
- Unchanged:
  - signed-tag and lane checks (`_verify_exact_tag_release_lane`);
  - the fresh protected-main fetch;
  - active/release reachability from main;
  - the ancestry-path merge scan;
  - lane CAS.

### Tests (`.agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-auto-sync.sh`)

- The GH#32103 `wrong-parent` topology (an intervening mainline commit) is now the accepted `intervening` deferral case. That is the real-world v3.37.3 shape.
- New `later-merge` rejection: the runtime reaches main only after the integration merge, so the integration's mainline parent does not contain it.
- `unreachable` rejection is retained.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-auto-sync.sh`: 37/37 passed. This includes the new intervening deferral and the `later-merge` and `unreachable` rejections.
- `shellcheck` is clean on both files, `linters-local.sh --changed` exits 0, and `qlty smells` reports no findings.

title: GH#32583: transport-neutral mesh remote workers; nvpn enrollment helper; NetBird/nvm dispatch fixes
body:
## Summary

This makes remote OpenCode workers over a private mesh a transport-neutral aidevops path, with setup tooling for Nostr VPN and fixes to the existing remote-dispatch path.

**`remote-dispatch-helper.sh`** (bug fixes)
- Adds transports `netbird|nvpn|wireguard` alongside `ssh|tailscale`. All of them use SSH; only `tailscale` switches to `tailscale ssh`.
- **Fixes misdetection**: any `100.x.x.x` address used to be classified as Tailscale, but NetBird shares `100.64.0.0/10`. A `100.x` address is now Tailscale or NetBird only when `tailscale status` or `netbird status -d` lists it. Otherwise it's plain SSH. `*.nvpn` and `*.netbird.*` names are detected too.
- **Fixes "no AI CLI" on nvm/bun installs**: `check` and dispatch ran `command -v opencode` in non-login SSH shells. A PATH preamble (user tool dirs plus nvm, `set -u`-safe) is now applied to detection and to the generated dispatch script.
- Prints mesh-specific diagnostics when SSH fails.

**`nostr-vpn-helper.sh` plus the new `nostr-vpn-setup-lib.sh`**: `setup-admin`, `join`, `approve`, `set-alias`, `aliases`, `dns-check`, `direct-only`. They turn the manual steps from #23846 into one command per device, and each prints the next command to run. Alias writes go to `[peer_aliases]` with a backup and `0600` permissions.

**Docs**
- New `reference/mesh-remote-workers.md`: mesh comparison ordered by decentralisation (Nostr VPN, self-hosted NetBird, Headscale, WireGuard/SSH, hosted Tailscale), joining machines, SSH, `remote-dispatch-helper` registration, and loopback-only OpenCode over `ssh -L`.
- `nostr-vpn.md`: helper-based enrollment, direct-only mode, the default third-party bootstrap peers and relays, and the finding that nvpn cannot run over NetBird.
- `netbird.md`: remote-worker and nvpn coexistence notes.
- `remote-dispatch.md`: transport table and trust note.
- `domain-index.md`: routing to the new reference.

## Live evidence (two Macs, nvpn 4.1.16 and self-hosted NetBird 0.79)

- `remote-dispatch-helper.sh add` auto-detected the real NetBird peer's `100.x` address as `netbird` and `mini.nvpn` as `nvpn`. `check` passed on both, with `OpenCode CLI: available`; the old non-login check had failed on the same nvm install.
- `direct-only` with LAN endpoints: `fips_bootstrap_enabled: false`, `fips_nostr_discovery_enabled: false`, `0 other` FIPS peers, and `ping mini.nvpn` with 0% loss. Restored to defaults afterwards.
- nvpn over NetBird: a CGNAT hint was rejected by nvpn. A NetBird IPv6 ULA hint failed with `No route to host (os error 65)` even though `ping6` worked; the daemon log shows `physical route sample: selected=en0`. Documented as "side by side, not layered".
- `setup-admin` and `approve` ran on the existing network (idempotent). `dns-check mini` passed all three layers. The mesh stayed up.
- Found and fixed during testing: a `pipefail` + `grep -q` SIGPIPE false negative (`scutil`, `netbird status -d`), and `aliases` dropping a final line with no trailing newline.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on all changed scripts: clean
- `test-nostr-vpn-helper.sh`: 17/17, including 5 new tests covering the config writer (replace, create section, reject invalid npub without touching config), direct-only CGNAT rejection and flags, and alias export.
- New `test-remote-dispatch-transport.sh`: 8/8, run through the real CLI with stubbed `tailscale`/`netbird`.
- `test-remote-dispatch-wrapper-sentinel.sh`: pass
- `linters-local.sh --changed`: exit 0

Resolves #32583
Ref #23846

title: t18487: allow remote-only repo creation from sessions inside the projects workspace
body:
## Summary

Interactive sessions under `~/Git` could not create a GitHub repository: the shared command policy required a per-command authorization digest inherited at runtime launch, so the maintainer had to create three Cloudron package repos by hand. Creating an empty repository from inside the projects workspace is routine and reversible, so it no longer needs a digest.

- `.agents/scripts/command_policy_account_mutation.py`: new `_is_workspace_repository_creation` exemption, checked before digest matching. It allows only a direct, unwrapped `gh repo create|new <name>` with explicit `--public|--private|--internal` and the existing remote-only allowlisted options, when the realpath of the session cwd is inside `AIDEVOPS_ACCOUNT_MUTATION_WORKSPACE_ROOT` (default `~/Git`).
- Still authorization-gated: forks, `--source`, `--clone`, `--push`, `--remote`, local templates, `sudo`/shell-launched forms, compound commands, sessions outside the root, sibling-prefix and symlink escapes, and an empty (disabled) workspace root.
- `.agents/scripts/command_policy_workspace.py` (new): workspace-root containment helpers and the direct-invocation check, moved out of the account-mutation module to keep it under the Qlty file-complexity threshold; existing names stay re-exported.
- `.agents/reference/gh-command-discipline.md`: documents the exemption.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-command-policy-helper.sh`: `test_workspace_repository_creation` covers allowed and still-gated forms.

Resolves #32600

## Security

`#aidevops:trust-boundary` gate changed deliberately at the user's request. The exemption can only allow the narrowest existing workspace-safe create form; it never widens fork, clone, source-push, or wrapped execution paths. Operators opt out with `AIDEVOPS_ACCOUNT_MUTATION_WORKSPACE_ROOT=""`.

title: GH#32633: fix(pulse): restore dispatch throughput — bounded scratch cleanup, cheap candidate rejection, routine failure backoff
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes four sources of per-cycle Pulse waste that were starving worker dispatch on every runner. Evidence and reproducer are in #32633.

- **Regression fix (GH#32485 / #32519, shipped in v3.37.5+):** `cleanup_stale_opencode` runs `system-cleanup.sh --force` synchronously, spawning one `trash` process per entry. With a 43k-entry scratch backlog it hit the 600s preflight timeout on every cycle. That delayed the first dispatch by about 10 minutes and skipped `cleanup_stalled_workers`, `reap_zombie_workers` and ledger expiry. The script now batches trash moves (200 per call), accepts a `--max-seconds` budget (Pulse passes 60s, via `PULSE_SCRATCH_CLEANUP_MAX_SECONDS`), and writes one summary line to the Pulse log instead of one line per entry.
- **Late-rejected candidates:** `hold-for-review` is excluded at candidate-build time. The dispatch-time policy gate stays as defence-in-depth. `terminal_blocker_circuit` rejections now use the existing cross-cycle negative cache, keyed on unchanged `updatedAt` with a 2h TTL, so any edit, retry directive or comment re-arms dispatch. Each of these rejections previously cost a 40-110s ceremony per runner per cycle (1,042 circuit rejections logged on one runner).
- **Failing routines:** consecutive routine failures back off exponentially (900s doubling, capped at 6h) and reset on success. Script routines run synchronously ahead of dispatch, so a failing daily routine used to re-run on almost every cycle.
- **Session miner:** target-level contributor deferrals (`public_target_unconfirmed`, `unknown_or_private_role`, `contributor_path_unavailable`) now skip that target instead of failing the whole miner run. Previously the miner re-ran its ~4-minute mining pass every 15 minutes.
- **Worker blocker guidance:** `workflows/full-loop.md` and `tools/ai-assistants/headless-dispatch.md` said "missing deps" was a reason to exit BLOCKED. Workers took that literally and gave up on a private web-app repo's tasks because a fresh worktree had no `tsx`, `@playwright/test` or pinned Node, burning 50-min leases. The guidance now says to install from the committed lockfile and select the pinned runtime first, and to block only if that install fails with evidence.
- **Redeploy churn:** every code commit to `main` triggered a same-version "script drift" redeploy on every runner (`auto-update.log`: 701 Pulse restarts). Each redeploy kills the in-flight Pulse cycle via `reconcile-managed`. With `main` moving every 20-40 minutes and cycles running 30-60 minutes, Pulse rarely reached dispatch (`pulse-watchdog.log`: "pulse dead for 5460s"). Same-version drift redeploys are now batched to at most one per hour, measured from the `.deployed-sha` mtime (`AIDEVOPS_SCRIPT_DRIFT_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, 0 disables batching). Releases, which change `VERSION`, still redeploy immediately. The change is applied to both `auto-update-helper.sh` and its `-check.sh` twin.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-routine-calendar-scheduling.sh`: 34/34, including 3 new backoff/reset assertions.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-session-miner-actuation.sh`, `test-pulse-candidate-enumeration-recovery.sh`, `test-pulse-stash-cleanup-nonblocking.sh`, `test-pulse-routines-selector.sh` and `test-routine-tracking-updates.sh`: all pass.
- `shellcheck` is clean on all changed scripts.
- `test-cmd-update-sha-drift.sh`: the 15 auto-update assertions pass. The 3 `aidevops.sh` assertions fail identically on `main` (pre-existing, unrelated).
- Debounce harness: a fresh stamp is batched; an old stamp or a window of `0` redeploys.
- Production path: `system-cleanup.sh --force --max-seconds 30` trashed 9,200 entries in 30s, versus more than 600s for a partial pass before. A 100s run then drained the remaining 16,086 eligible entries in 47s.
- Production path: `session-miner-actuation-helper.sh contributor` against a private contributor target now returns `deferred/public_target_unconfirmed` with exit 0.
- Ad-hoc harness checks of the negative cache: a same-`updatedAt` circuit is a hit; a changed `updatedAt`, an expired TTL or an unowned active-claim record is a miss. The candidate filter drops only the `hold-for-review` issue.

Resolves #32633

title: GH#32663: feat(pulse): auto worker cap (50% of cores) with one-time fleet reset of capacity overrides
body:
## Summary

Resolves #32663

This PR makes the Pulse worker ceiling an auto value: 50% of logical CPU cores, bounded by RAM and clamped to [2, 64]. It also ships a one-time setup migration that resets hand-tuned capacity overrides on every install, so auto-update rolls the new default out to the whole fleet with no manual steps. This follows the maintainer's decision to do a one-time reset of all custom capacity settings now that #32634 fixed the throughput problems.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh`:
  - the auto cap is `hw.logicalcpu` (macOS) or `nproc` (Linux) divided by 2, then min'd with the RAM cap;
  - a config value of `0`, `auto` or empty selects auto;
  - the floor is lowered from 4 to 2 so small hosts are not over-subscribed.
- `.agents/configs/aidevops.defaults.jsonc`, `.agents/configs/aidevops-config.schema.json`: `max_workers_cap` now defaults to `0` (auto).
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`: `min_worker_concurrency` is clamped to `MAX_WORKERS_CAP`, so the refill floor never pushes past the host ceiling.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity-alloc.sh`: the macOS reclaimable RAM estimate now also counts speculative and purgeable pages. Busy Macs were under-reporting headroom.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh`: new `migrate_worker_capacity_reset`, following the pattern of `migrate_custom_model_routing_reasoning_defaults`. It:
  - removes `orchestration.max_workers_cap`, `min_worker_concurrency` and `provider_account_slot_multiplier` via `config-helper.sh reset`;
  - strips capacity env keys from `plist-env-overrides.json`;
  - writes backups to `~/.aidevops/config-backups/migrations/gh32663-*`;
  - writes a one-time marker to `~/.aidevops/cache/migrations/gh32663-worker-capacity-reset`, so explicit settings made later are honoured;
  - warns (without editing) if `credentials.sh` exports a capacity override;
  - leaves symlinked files untouched.
- `setup.sh`: runs the migration in both the non-interactive (auto-update) path and the interactive path.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on all changed shell files: clean.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`: all local checks passed. The shfmt advisories are pre-existing drift on main; unrelated reformatting was deliberately left out.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-count.sh`: 42/42 pass.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-model-routing-reasoning-migration.sh`: all pass.
- Auto cap harness on a 16-core, 128 GB Mac:
  - unset config gives `MAX_WORKERS_CAP=8`;
  - `0` gives `8`;
  - an explicit `12` gives `12`.
- Migration harness in a sandbox HOME:
  - it removed `max_workers_cap: 2` and `min_worker_concurrency: 1`, left unrelated keys intact, and stripped `AIDEVOPS_MAX_WORKERS_CAP` while keeping `AIDEVOPS_MODEL_AB_CONFIG`;
  - it wrote both backups and the marker;
  - a second run left a newly set explicit value untouched.

## Notes

- Hosts that had tuned values above `cores/2` will drop, for example 24 to 8 on a 16-core host. This is the intended one-time reset. Operators can raise the value again with `aidevops config set orchestration.max_workers_cap N` after the migration runs.
- The user JSONC config is regenerated by `config-helper.sh reset`, which drops user comments. The original is kept in the backup.

title: GH#32683: fix(setup): keep migration backups when cleaning legacy config-backups
body:
## Summary

Resolves #32683

`migrate_old_backups` runs first on every `setup.sh` run. It used to `rm -rf ~/.aidevops/config-backups` whenever that directory had no legacy `20*` snapshots. That also deleted `config-backups/migrations/`, where the one-time migrations (model-routing reasoning defaults, obsolete settings routing, legacy AGENTS.md, worker-capacity reset) keep their pre-change backups, so each backup lasted only until the next auto-update deploy.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh` (`migrate_old_backups`):
  - removes only legacy `20*` snapshot directories;
  - removes the parent with `rmdir`, and only when it is empty.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-model-routing-reasoning-migration.sh`: after the t18137 migration writes its backup, runs `migrate_old_backups` and asserts the backup survives.

## Verification

body:
<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Marcus Quinn -->

Resolves #32644

## Outcome

The brief explicitly permits reporting usage without changing code when no eligible
registered tool meets the threshold. Keep the existing dispatcher list. The earlier
attempt to add native session-title names did not defer them and is removed; no
API-token saving is claimed for that ineffective change.

## Measured selection

Read-only 30-day session-use measurement on 2026-10-03: 2,010 active sessions.

| Tool | Sessions | Percent | Disposition |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| ai-research | 119 | 5.920 | Above 2% |
| aidevops | 175 | 8.706 | Above 2% |
| aidevops_bounded_operation | 734 | 36.517 | Above 2% |
| aidevops_hook_status | 289 | 14.378 | Above 2% |
| aidevops_mcp | 104 | 5.174 | Above 2%; agent-gated |
| aidevops_memory | 1,169 | 58.159 | Mandatory recall |
| aidevops_pre_edit_check | 486 | 24.179 | Mandatory safety step |
| session-rename | 245 | 12.189 | Above 2%; native registration |
| session-rename_sync_branch | 33 | 1.642 | Native registration, not in baseTools |

`moveToolsOnDemand` operates on the plugin's `baseTools`; `.opencode/tool/`
exports are registered separately. Names absent from that map are ignored.
Changing their list membership would therefore not remove their tool definitions.
The documentation adds the reproducible distinct-session query, correctly comparing
ISO UTC timestamps rather than SQLite's space-separated datetime format.

## Provider-native deferral

Do not enable provider-native deferral here. OpenCode 1.18.34's reviewed
`packages/opencode/src/session/llm/native-request.ts` normalizes the tool record
to its native `ToolDefinition[]` and selects the Anthropic/OpenAI transports;
the exported plugin/SDK 1.18.33 interfaces do not supply a provider-native
deferred-tool registration capability. The existing plugin dispatcher remains
the verified route. This establishes the host integration boundary, not a claim
that either provider API can never support deferred tools.

title: GH#32700: fix(opencode-v2): restore exact V2 sessions in restored Tabby tabs
body:
## Summary

When Tabby restores a tab, OpenCode V2 (`opencode2`) now reopens the exact session that was in it.

- **V2 TUI plugin** (`v2-plugin/tui.mjs`): V2 server plugins run in the background service, which has no tty. So the TUI process now writes a schema-2 `runtime: "v2"` recovery marker for the routed root session and reports it to Tabby with `OSC 1337 CurrentDir`. Switching sessions rewrites the marker.
- **`opencode2` shim** (`setup/modules/tool-install.sh`, shim version 3): launching from a valid V2 marker resumes `--session <id>` in the session's directory. It opens the directory without resuming when:
  - the owner TUI is still live (split or duplicated tab);
  - the caller passed `--session` or `--continue`;
  - the marker is V1.

  After a normal exit it reports the project directory back to Tabby. A hangup (Tabby quit or crash) leaves the marker in place for restoration. Opt out with `AIDEVOPS_TABBY_V2_RECOVERY=0`.
- **Resolver** (`session-recovery-marker.mjs`):
  - validates V2 markers against the caller's V2 data home and the `session_v2` table;
  - returns exit `4` with the directory only for cross-runtime markers, so neither runtime resumes the other's session;
  - adds a `ps -o lstart=` liveness fallback. Without it, `ownerLive` was always false on macOS, so the GH#32482 split-tab guard never fired there.
- **V1 launcher**: handles exit `4` by opening the V2 marker's project directory.
- **Docs**: `.agents/reference/tabby-profiles.md` gains an "OpenCode V2" section.

Resolves #32700

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk:** High (session restore/launch path)
- **Level:** runtime-verified
- **Shim:** I generated a real `opencode2` shim with a fake wrapper and ran it against a real sqlite `session_v2` DB:
  - marker dir → `--session <id>` run in the session directory;
  - `--continue` is preserved;
  - live owner → opens the directory only, no resume;
  - non-Tabby → recovery off;
  - no tty → no output.
- **Resolver CLI:** exercised with real markers; exit codes 0, 3 and 4 as expected.
- `node .agents/scripts/tests/test-session-recovery-marker.mjs` passes. It failed on macOS before this change.
- `test-opencode-v2-tui-title.mjs`: 8/8 pass.
- `test-opencode-launcher-helper.sh`: all Tabby cases pass. Two unrelated failures are identical on main; they come from the V2 session's inherited `XDG_DATA_HOME`.
- Plugin `npm run test`: passes apart from load-flaky timing tests, which pass when run individually:
  - `test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs`: 13/13
  - `test-signature-footer-gate.mjs`: 82/82

  `test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs` also reads the real `~/.config/aidevops/settings.json`, which makes it non-hermetic. This is pre-existing.
- `shellcheck` is clean.
- `tui.mjs` imports under Bun.
- The in-Tabby end-to-end check follows deploy.

## Decisions

- Schema 1 stays V1-only, so older resolvers reject V2 markers instead of misreading them.
- Markers from the other runtime never resume a session.
- The shim runs the TUI without `exec` only while Tabby recovery is active. Post-exit reporting therefore runs only on a normal exit, never on a hangup.

title: t18506: persistent dashboards — accurate, privacy-minimal, public-readable (GH#32730)
body:
## Summary

Makes the persistent dashboard issues accurate, safe to publish on public repositories, and readable by collaborators and the public. Adds `reference/persistent-dashboards.md` as the written contract for what these issues contain, who reads them, and how they are maintained.

Resolves #32730

## Evidence (live audit, 2026-09-28)

- `Code Audit Routines` title rendered as `Open: 1 | Closed: 2039 | Simplified: | Metric | Count |`. `Badge status` was empty, and `Bot Review Coverage` showed only its heading.
- The quality dashboard carried `auto-dispatch` + `status:available` + `tier:standard`. It collected about 85 NMR decision packets, dispatch claims and a `missing_files_scope` blocker, for a total of 205 comments.
- Health dashboard bodies published provider credential posture (`OpenAI: oauth; Anthropic: missing; auth file: present`). They also published raw JSONL/TSV telemetry (session, worker, run and attempt IDs, PIDs, model) and host fingerprinting (cores, free memory, process count), and listed identity aliases. The memory row read `low (83785MB free)`, where `low` meant low pressure.
- `whoami` fallback identities produced `[Contributor:vladimir]`, `[Contributor:alexey]` and `[Contributor:vod]` with the wrong role. They are now 19–27 days stale.

## Changes

**Quality dashboard** (`stats-quality-sweep-issues.sh`, `stats-quality-sweep.sh`)
- Stats transport between gather and render is now NUL-delimited, which fixes the shifted badge, simplified and title fields (root cause of the broken title).
- The title now carries public signals: `Code Audit Routines — Qlty C (82 smells) · Sonar OK · quality debt: 1 open, 2039 closed`. The invariant prefix used by dedup is unchanged.
- `_normalize_quality_issue_labels` removes `auto-dispatch`/`no-auto-dispatch`/`status:*`/`tier:*` on each update. `needs-maintainer-review` is never touched (trust boundary).
- `_minimize_superseded_dashboard_comments` hides superseded automation comments as OUTDATED after each sweep. These are older sweep comments, NMR packets, ops audit comments and worker launch notes. At most 50 are hidden per run, and hiding is reversible. Human comments, signed approvals and bot reviews are never selected.
- The body gains a one-line explanation for readers.

**Health dashboards** (`stats-health-dashboard*.sh`)
- Diagnostics show `Model access: available|unavailable`, and `Last worker run`/`Last dispatch stage` as time · issue · outcome · duration only. Evidence is scoped to the dashboard's own repository, because the logs are shared with private repositories.
- The `System Resources` section is replaced by a coarse `Host pressure: CPU <level> · memory <level>` summary row, which also fixes the mislabel.
- The body shows the canonical operator but not the alias list. The creation body no longer lists aliases either.
- Sections with no data are omitted instead of rendering `_… unavailable._` placeholders. The PR table is labelled repository-wide.
- Dashboards publish under the scheduler-verified GitHub login. They never publish under a `whoami` fallback or `unknown-runner`.
- The supervisor archives other operators' dashboards whose `last_refresh:` is older than 14 days (`HEALTH_STALE_DASHBOARD_SECONDS`, minimum 7 days). It strips `persistent` first and scans at most once a day. A returning operator's stats process recreates its dashboard automatically.
- Label normalization also removes `tier:*`.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x` on all changed scripts: clean. `linters-local.sh --changed`: string-literal, function-complexity, bash32, markdown and secretlint gates pass.
- Tests pass: `test-stats-quality-sweep-issues.sh` (16, with new cases for multi-line transport, title and comment selection), `test-stats-worker-zero-diagnostics.sh` (4, including repository scoping and no auth/telemetry leakage), `test-health-dashboard-identity-aliases.sh` (38, including stale-archive selection), `test-stats-wrapper-timeout.sh`, `test-health-dashboard-sentinel-abstain.sh`, `test-stats-functions-characterization.sh`, `test-dashboard-freshness-check.sh`.
- Pre-existing failures, identical on `main`: `test-create-health-issue-origin-label.sh` (2) and `test-stats-wrapper-headless-export.sh` (3).
- Rendered the real `marcusquinn/aidevops` health body locally from live data. It contains no IDs, auth posture, aliases, cores or process counts, and no placeholder sections.
- Dry-ran the stale selector against live issues: #26416, #25313 and #24173 qualify at 14 days. The current operator's dashboard is excluded.

## Follow-up

- The `marcusquinn/aidevops` quality sweep exceeds its 120s per-repository budget (`rc=124` on every attempt since 2026-09-05), so its dashboard never refreshes. Filed as #32737 (auto-dispatch).

title: t18510: fix(setup): keep V1 plugin pass out of the live OpenCode V2 config
body:
## Summary

An OpenCode V2 session failed mid-session with `AI.Error.Authentication: API key is invalid.`

**Root cause:** the session ran `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-v2-setup.sh`, which isolates only `HOME`. The opencode2 shim exports `OPENCODE_CONFIG`, `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` for the live V2 runtime. The test's `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE=v1 setup_opencode_runtime_plugins` took the V1 branch, which, unlike the V2-selected branch, does not strip V2 ambient config. `find_opencode_config` and the V1 plugins dir therefore resolved to the **live** V2 config.

The live `opencode.json` was rewritten to a V1 `plugin` entry into the mktemp sandbox, plus a dangling `plugins/opencode-aidevops` link. Six seconds later V2 hot-reloaded it, and the plugin failed to load. First `Agent not found: "Build+"`, then the OAuth pool `http.request` hook was missing, so requests went out with the placeholder key.

Evidence (V2 `opencode.log`): the test ran at 02:21:38Z (session DB tool call); `failed to load plugin target=/var/folders/.../aidevops-opencode-v2-setup.XXXXXX.rpKrOULVVI/...` at 02:21:44Z; `API key is invalid` at 02:23:19Z.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh`: V1 path resolution (`_setup_opencode_v1_ambient_path`, `_setup_opencode_v1_find_config`) ignores ambient config paths owned by the aidevops V2 runtime root. User-chosen V1 `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`OPENCODE_CONFIG` stay honoured. The V2 pass removes a setup-managed V1 `opencode-aidevops` link from the V2 plugins dir, so a redeploy repairs residue.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-v2-setup.sh`: unsets ambient OpenCode/XDG/V2 env at start. A new regression check runs a V1-only pass under simulated V2 ambient env and asserts the V2 config is untouched, then runs the V2 pass and asserts the residue link is removed.
- `TODO.md`: t18510 entry.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium (setup config writes)
- **Verification:** runtime-verified
  - Reproduced the live corruption with unfixed `main` under a simulated opencode2 env pointing at a decoy V2 root. The decoy was rewritten to `"plugin": [..., "file:///var/folders/.../aidevops-opencode-v2-setup.../index.mjs"]` plus the dangling link, identical to the live incident.
  - With the fix: the test passes under the same simulated env and the decoy config is unchanged.
  - The new regression assertion fails against the old `mcp-setup.sh` (`V1 plugin pass rewrote the V2 config from ambient V2 env`) and passes with the fix.
  - Live V1/V2 `opencode.json` hashes were unchanged across all test runs.
  - `test-setup-scoped-dispatch.sh` (60/60) and `test-macos-automator-platform-filter.sh` (6/6) pass; `linters-local.sh --changed` passes; shellcheck is clean.
- Live V2 config was repaired manually. V2 hot-reloaded it (`config.updated`/`agent.updated`, no plugin load errors).

Resolves #32738

title: GH#32744: Anthropic prompt-cache stability, truthful profile cache stats, compaction re-read guidance
body:
## Summary

Pins the resolved greeting block per session so release deploys stop rewriting the cached framework prefix of every open session; adds a fail-open cache-stability monitor that logs which request segment (account/tools/system/thinking/prefix/history) changed when a cache break happens; fixes profile README cache hit rate (cache writes now count as prompt tokens, new Cache write column, dated model IDs merged into one row) and adds desktop/server OpenCode data homes to session-time discovery; adds a concise Working set section to compaction guidance and corrects the Read-before-Edit rule to avoid needless post-compaction re-reads. Claude compaction target unchanged by decision.

## Changes

### Greeting pinning (`ttsr.mjs`)
- `pinSessionGreeting()` caches the resolved greeting per session; the new test confirms an open session replays identical bytes after `VERSION` changes
- Prevents VERSION-only deploys from rewriting the cached framework prefix of every open session (56 post-GH#32444 turns re-wrote cache within 5 minutes of the prior turn, ~$67 total)

### Cache-stability diagnostics (`cache-stability.mjs`, new)
- Per-request, per-session fingerprint of account/tools/system/thinking/prefix/history segments; never mutates the request
- Logs the first changed stable segment on a break; disable with `AIDEVOPS_CACHE_STABILITY_LOG=0`
- Wired into `provider-auth-body.mjs`; `provider-auth.mjs` passes the account

### Profile README fixes
- **Hit-rate formula**: `cache_read / (input + cache_write + cache_read)`; cache writes were omitted, overstating Claude rows as 100%
- **Cache write column** added to model usage tables
- **Dated model IDs** (e.g. `claude-opus-4-6-20250610`) merge with their alias into one row; session hours stay unknown if any merged row lacks them
- **Session-time discovery** includes `opencode-desktop/*` and `opencode-server/*` data homes (5 additional DBs on the test machine)
- Row rendering split into `_render_model_usage_row` to stay under the complexity gate

### Compaction guidance (`compaction.mjs`)
- Adds a concise Working set section (edit targets with anchors, established results, reusable artifacts)
- Clarifies the Read-before-Edit rule so established content is not needlessly re-read after compaction

## Testing

- `node --test`: test-cache-stability, test-ttsr-system-transform (new pin case), test-provider-auth-cch, test-compaction-checkpoint-scope, test-compaction-autocontinue, test-token-advisory-threshold — 37/37 pass
- `test-profile-readme-boundary.sh`: 27/27 with updated cache-write and dated-alias expectations
- `profile-readme-helper.sh generate` against local DBs: claude-opus-5-5 now 96.7% (was 100.0%) with 119.6M cache write; one row per model
- `session_time_db.db_paths` probe: 34 interactive + 2 desktop + 3 server data homes
- shellcheck clean; `linters-local.sh --changed` pass
- Runtime probe (runtime-verified): `opencode run` with an isolated config whose `plugin` entry points at this branch's `index.mjs`, `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` via OAuth, one prompt forcing two Read tool calls, so two Anthropic requests in one session. Request 1: cache_write 21,633 / cache_read 0. Request 2: cache_read 21,633 / cache_write 833 (only the new tool results). No `cache-stability:` break lines. The mid-session VERSION-change pin is covered by the unit test, not this probe: the pin and monitor are in-process, so a cross-process `--continue` probe cannot exercise them.

## Decisions

- **Diagnostics before speculative fixes**: tools-level (cache_read=0) and history-level breaks could not be attributed from existing logs, so the monitor records the changed segment instead of guessing

title: t18513: fix quality dashboard comment hygiene no-op on large threads (GH#32752)

## Summary

Pages were merged with `jq --argjson` using full comment bodies. On #24670 (205 comments, multi-KB sweep reports), the argument exceeded the OS argument-size limit. The function then hit `|| return 0` without logging.

title: GH#32624: Deduplicate Build+ shared prompt rules
body:
Resolves #32624

Deduplicate Build+ rules already owned by `.agents/AGENTS.md`. Keep Build+-specific intent detection, workflow, lookup, domain routing, and stricter full-repository-gate guidance. No change to the shared guide; it is 23,993 bytes against the 24,000-byte CI ratchet.

### Overlap decisions (old Build+ line → shared owner)

| Topic | Old Build+ | Shared guide | Relation and decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| Memory recall | 125 | 67 | Same; point Build+ step 2 to shared mandatory recall. |
| Adding tests | 131 | 62 | Same; point Build+ step 8 to shared test policy; keep product-path/log verification. |
| Subagent critical path | 104 | 53, 56 | Same; point to shared rule; retain Build+-specific effort tiers and no nested delegation. |
| File re-read | 117, 129 | 81 | Shared is stricter (read before every edit); remove weaker instruction. |
| Untrusted content | 124 | 95 | Same; point to shared security rule; keep scanner-warning response and external lookup table. |
| Response style | 118 | 42, 80, 84 | Same; remove Build+ wording, leave shared prose/file discipline. |
| Quality gates | 115, 131 | 62, 130–131 | Shared owns baseline; retain Build+ full-repository blast-radius distinction and UI-specific workflow. |
| Pre-edit check | 99 | 29 | Shared is stricter and handles pre-created worktrees; point execution step there. |
| Commit safety | 113 | 99, 112–115 | Contradiction: delete “NEVER auto-commit”; shared WIP commits are authorized linked-worktree checkpoints, not unsolicited commits of a user's unrelated work. Destructive operations still require the shared safety rule. |
| Search and GitHub lookup | 114, 127 | 80, 97 | Same exact-search/URL guards; keep Build+-specific semantic-search escalation and external lookup table. |

title: GH#32825: Align compaction guidance with OpenCode 1/2 host summary templates
body:
## Summary

Our compaction guidance asked for its own headings (## Session aims, ## Continuation state, ## Working set). Both OpenCode hosts impose a fixed summary template and retry or reject off-template output, so the host format won and our objective-state marker was dropped (seen in a real OpenCode 1.18.33 compaction in the GH#32807 session). This maps aidevops rules onto each host's sections instead: Objective gets one bullet per user aim with status and the user's defining words verbatim (overriding the host's one-or-two-sentence limit); the details section carries constraints, decisions with evidence, input not yet applied, point-in-time labels and the labelled session-analysis evidence group; Work State carries proof and worktree/branch/commit plus push/PR/merge/release state; Next Move starts with ACTIVE/DELIVERED/EXTERNALLY_BLOCKED and Continuation required: yes with the exact next command; Relevant Files carries line anchors and reusable artifacts. The details-section name is mapped per host (OpenCode 1 Important Details; OpenCode 2 Requirements/Decisions/Important Context). Rules the hosts already enforce (terse bullets, exact identifiers, prior-summary merge) and the Critical Rules to Preserve block are dropped: hosts re-send system prompts and AGENTS.md after compaction and OpenCode 2 explicitly excludes them. Guidance payload drops from about 1,500 to 750 tokens. session.md and session-analysis.md describe the host-aligned format.



## Files Changed

.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-compaction-checkpoint-scope.mjs, .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs, .agents/reference/session.md, .agents/workflows/session-analysis.md

title: docs(session): continuation-reminder issues for sessions waiting on background work
body:
## Summary

Sessions often hand issues to pulse/workers and then stay open only to wait for them. This adds a "Continuation Reminders" rule to `.agents/reference/session.md` so the session can close instead:

- One self-assigned issue labelled `continuation-reminder` + `no-auto-dispatch` (humans resume it; workers never do).
- Title `Continue: <aim>`, with an optional `(check <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM>)` when a check-back time is known.
- Body holds the aim, delivered evidence, outstanding aims, resume action, worktree/branch and verification.
- `blocked-by:#N` markers plus native `addBlockedBy` edges, so the reminder becomes actionable once the last dependency closes.
- Capture Check step 5 points to it; the What Next **Session** line cites it, and the session counts as `Ready to close`.

`no-auto-dispatch` is already a hold in `dependency-event-reconciler.sh` (`_der_labels_have_hold`), so unblocking never exposes the reminder to worker dispatch.
