title: GH#32848: adopt Claude Sonnet 5.5 as Sonnet default with one-time settings migration
body:
## Summary

Claude Sonnet 5.5 (`claude-sonnet-5-5`) was released on 2026-09-28. It costs the same as Sonnet 5 ($2 in, $10 out, $0.20 cache read per 1M tokens), runs 30%+ faster, and uses fewer tokens per task (source: Anthropic's launch page). This PR makes it the Sonnet default across aidevops and migrates existing user pins once.

## Changes

- **Defaults**: current-default `claude-sonnet-4-6` and bare `claude-sonnet-5` IDs become `claude-sonnet-5-5` in configs, scripts, docs and tests (`model-routing-table.json`, `aidevops.defaults.jsonc`, `shared-model-tier.sh`, `headless-runtime-helper.sh`, and others).
- **Catalogs** (5.5 added next to the old entries, not replacing them):
  - `model-pricing.json`: `sonnet-5-5` key placed before `sonnet-5`. The pricing version is unchanged because the rates are identical.
  - `model-limits.mjs`: new entry.
  - `config-hook.mjs`: CLI name.
  - `claude-proxy-context.mjs`: the `sonnet` alias now maps to 5-5.
  - `compare-models-helper.sh`: new row.
  - `models-sonnet.md` and `model-routing.md`: updated.
- **OpenCode catalog bridge** (`anthropic-catalog-bridge.mjs`): models.dev does not list `claude-sonnet-5-5` yet, so `opencode run -m anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` currently fails with `ProviderModelNotFoundError`. The bridge registers pending IDs using Sonnet 5 metadata only when the catalog lacks them and the user has not defined them. Once models.dev publishes the model, the native entry wins. Live check: with the definition injected, OpenCode headless answered correctly at the default and `medium` variants.
- **One-time migration** (`setup/modules/migration-sonnet-5-5.sh`, marker `gh32848-sonnet-5-5-settings`):
  - Rewrites provider-prefixed Sonnet 4.6/5 pins in `~/.config/aidevops/config.jsonc`, `settings.json`, `plist-env-overrides.json`, the custom routing table, and `opencode.json(c)`.
  - In `credentials.sh` and tenant credential files, it changes only `*_MODEL(S)=` lines.
  - It backs up each file to `~/.aidevops/config-backups/migrations/` and skips symlinks.
- History is unchanged: CHANGELOG, TODO.md, `todo/`, and dated pricing keys.

## Caveats (documented in `models-sonnet.md`)

- Turning thinking off requires the `between_tools` setting. No aidevops code path currently disables thinking for Sonnet.
- High-risk cyber requests fall back to Sonnet 5.
- The installed Claude Code catalog warns that the ID is unknown and assumes a 200K window.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-sonnet-5-5-migration.sh`: 28/28 pass.
- `node --test` on `test-model-limits.mjs` and `test-observability-pricing.mjs`: 29/29 pass.

- The broader shell and plugin suites match the `main` baseline. The failures that already exist on `main` are tracked in #32852 and are unrelated to this change.

Resolves #32848

title: GH#32858: fix(source-access): macOS bundle ACL uses account name, not numeric uid
body:
## Summary

private_bundle_parent() passed 'user:<uid> allow ...' to /bin/chmod -E on Darwin; macOS rejects numeric uids ('Unable to translate 501 to a UUID'), so every V3 bundle approval failed with 'private bundle ACL setup failed' once #32834 let state creation succeed. Darwin now resolves the uid to its login name, requires it to round-trip via getpwnam to the same uid and match a strict name pattern (no newline/colon/whitespace injection), then emits user:<name>. macOS binds the ACE to that account's UUID. Linux setfacl path unchanged.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/source_access_core.py, .agents/scripts/tests/test-source-access-bundle-acl.py, .agents/scripts/tests/test-source-access-helper.sh, .github/workflows/plugin-import-check.yml

title: GH#32880: fail closed on unscoped auto-dispatch issues from the gh_create_issue shim
body:
## Summary

Root cause of most current `status:blocked` issues: agents published `auto-dispatch` briefs without a canonical Files Scope. The pulse then held them as `missing_files_scope`. `_gh_ci_validate_dispatch_scope` only printed a warning for bodies with no scope declarations at all, and agents did not act on it. On 2026-09-28, 7 of 12 blocked issues were this class, all created after the GH#32598 warning shipped: #32849, #32826, #32760, #32745, #32737, #32721, and the legacy #20781. Their briefs have been repaired and returned to `status:available`.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh`: new `_gh_ci_dispatch_scope_strict` (`AIDEVOPS_STRICT_DISPATCH_SCOPE=1`). In strict mode, an unscoped `auto-dispatch` body fails creation (rc 1) with an actionable error. Otherwise the current warning is kept.
- `.agents/bin/gh_create_issue`: the agent-facing PATH shim defaults strict mode on, so interactive and headless agent calls fail closed before publishing. Scripts and routines that source the library keep warn-only behaviour, so scheduled finding-filers never lose findings. `AIDEVOPS_STRICT_DISPATCH_SCOPE=0` restores the warning at the shim.
- `.agents/workflows/brief.md` section 6: documents the refusal. It also tells authors to scope any test file that a required CI gate will demand (the #32723 `files_scope_excluded` class).
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-dispatch-validator.sh`: strict vs routine vs scoped vs non-dispatch cases, plus end-to-end runs through the shim with a recording `gh` stub (refusal, and the opt-out control).

Design note: #32880 proposed detecting the runtime from the environment (`OPENCODE`/`CLAUDECODE`). I rejected that because every local test run inside OpenCode inherits those variables: `test-gh-create-issue-auto-dispatch-skip.sh` and `test-origin-label-mutex-create.sh` failed locally with that approach. Scoping strictness to the PATH shim is deterministic and has no test blast radius.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Low (the refusal applies only to shim calls with `auto-dispatch` and no scope declarations at all)
- **Verification:**
  - `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-dispatch-validator.sh`: all pass, including the 3 new assertions.
  - `test-gh-create-issue-auto-dispatch-skip.sh`, `test-origin-label-mutex-create.sh`, `test-agent-bin-shim-sync.sh`, `test-shared-gh-wrappers-standalone.sh`: all pass.

Resolves #32880

title: GH#32871: fix(recovery): let opt-in CWD inspector read same-user setuid-root helpers
body:
## Summary

Stock Ubuntu/GNOME desktops kept `cwd-visibility-degraded` even after the operator installed the opt-in root inspector. The inspector rejected any process whose four `Uid:` fields differed, but the guard only skips processes whose four UIDs *all* differ. Same-user setuid-root helpers (ruid = user, euid/suid = 0), such as a FUSE mount's `fusermount3 auto_unmount` watcher or an open `sudo` parent, were therefore neither skippable nor inspectable.

- `worktree-cwd-inspect.py`: new pure `uid_fields_accepted()`. The real UID must be `SUDO_UID`; the effective, saved and filesystem UIDs must be `SUDO_UID` or `0`. It is applied before and after the `readlink`. A root real UID and any foreign UID are still refused.
- `audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh`: `_worktree_proc_entry_is_inspectable_uid` mirrors the rule. `list_worktree_unreadable_proc_cwds` now emits `<pid>\t<comm>\t<remedy>` (`inspector` | `stop-only`).
- `worktree-recovery-lifecycle-helper.sh`: the `unreadable-processes` header explains the REMEDY column.
- `worktree-recovery-maintenance-helper.sh`: the process-visibility advisory now names `worktree-helper.sh recovery unreadable-processes`.
- Docs: `reference/worktree-cwd-visibility.md` and `reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`.

Unchanged: `_capture_worktree_proc_cwds` degraded semantics, plan classification, and deletion authority. Extra visibility can only add positive (blocking) matches.

## Security notes

- The root inspector now discloses the CWD **path**, and only the path, of a setuid-root process whose real UID is the caller. It is never cross-user, and `SUDO_UID` stays sudo-managed and non-zero.
- An older installed inspector keeps the stricter rule, which fails closed. Operators must reinstall from the release to gain the new rule.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-removal-audit-lib.sh`: 58/58, including the new `privileged_inspector_uid_rule` (accepts `u u u u`, `u 0 0 0` and `u 0 0 u`; rejects `u v v v`, `0 u u u`, `0 0 0 0`, `u u u v`, 3-field, non-numeric, and a sudo UID of 0).
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-recovery-lifecycle.sh`: 58/58, including the extended listing fixture (`inspector` / `stop-only`) and the advisory naming the diagnostic.
- ShellCheck is clean on all changed shell files. `python3 -m py_compile` passes. `linters-local.sh --changed` passes; the only shfmt advisories are on unchanged lines.

title: GH#32955: t18537: retry policy helper once on ETIMEDOUT under host load; label second timeout as transient
body:
## Summary

The OpenCode command and canonical-write hooks ran their python3 policy helpers with a fixed 10 s timeout. Under host load (load average ~23 on 16 cores; a normal worker network check takes 2.75 s wall because it spawns network-tier-helper, jq and a second Python), 10 retained September worker excerpts show 17 blocks of the form "BLOCKED: command policy failed closed: spawnSync python3 ETIMEDOUT", which reads like a policy decision. A shared runPolicyHelper now reads the base timeout from AIDEVOPS_POLICY_HELPER_TIMEOUT_MS (default 10000) and, on ETIMEDOUT only, retries once at 3x. A second timeout still fails closed but says it is a transient infrastructure timeout, not a policy decision, and tells the worker to retry the same command.

The runner lives in a new quality-hooks-policy-runner.mjs module so quality-hooks-git-safety.mjs stays under the Qlty file-complexity threshold. The canonical-write failure message is unchanged.
